seel.name: Seel Schreibwaren
seel.summary: Website, CMS, custom form backend, hosting and ongoing operations — since 2022.
seel.subtitle: A stationery shop in the heart of Heilbronn — the website, the CMS, a custom backend, hosted in Europe.

client.heading: The client
client.body: Seel Schreibwaren sells stationery, office, art and craft supplies in Heilbronn's city centre. They wanted a website they could keep up to date themselves — new arrivals, events, the product range — without calling a developer for every change.

built.heading: What we built
items: A fast, statically generated website (Next.js) in German and English, with pages for news, events, the product range, services, the team, careers and more.
A self-hosted headless CMS so the shop edits its own content. Edits are published automatically on a schedule, and every image is optimised at build time.
The school-list service: a paper process turned into an online one — more on that below.
Local SEO: dedicated landing pages for Heilbronn and 19 surrounding towns, plus structured metadata on every page.

items.text: School-list service: parents order the school's stationery list online
Migration to TypeScript and the Next.js App Router
Move to Scaleway with Terraform, new school-list backend, CMS upgrade with a verified data migration, English version

hosting.heading: Hosted in Europe
hosting.body: The whole stack — website, CMS and backend — runs on Scaleway, a European cloud provider under EU jurisdiction. Customer and form data never leave Europe, and nothing depends on a US hyperscaler. Digital sovereignty by default, not as an add-on.

schoolList.heading: From paper list to online order
paragraphs: Every summer, schools in the region hand out a list of the stationery each child needs for the coming year. Parents used to bring that sheet into the shop.

Now they photograph or scan the list and upload it on seel-schreibwaren.de, add the details that matter — the child's name, left- or right-handed, colour and favourite-animal wishes, whether items should be labelled — and choose pickup or delivery. The shop receives everything in one email, assembles the set, and the parent gets an automatic confirmation.
A small change for parents, a big one for the shop: the busiest weeks of the year now arrive as structured requests instead of paper sheets at the counter.
